row.평가 축: 에이전트(임바디드 스킬 활용 물리 과제 수행)
row.정의: LLM 에이전트가 관측-행동 폐루프에서 임바디드 스킬(행동 133, 지각 20, 경험 97, 총 250개, 리소스 1,052건에서 구축)을 활용해 물리 조작 과제를 수행하는 정도를 평가하는 벤치마크. 평가 세트 Clean100은 LIBERO-Pro 기본 과제 25개에 언어·객체·과제·교체 교란 4종을 곱한 100개 과제(L10 24, Goal 28, Object 24, Spatial 24)로 구성된다. 세 가지 모드(네이티브 제어, 스킬 전용 실행, Agent-Directed Reuse)를 지원하며, 성공률과 함께 행동 수, 토큰, 소요 시간(분)을 기록한다. 논문 수치는 시드 26 기준 4개 에이전트 비교이며 현재 전역 리더보드가 아니다.
row.대표 과제: Clean100(LIBERO-Pro 100개 과제 사례)에서 네이티브 제어, 스킬 전용, Agent-Directed Reuse 모드 비교
row.대표 예시·설명: 영어 지시문 "put both moka pots on the stove"(LIBERO-10 객체 교란)처럼, 에이전트가 장면·손목 RGB 관측을 보고 스킬 또는 네이티브 로봇 제어를 호출해 두 물체를 차례로 옮기는 과제 설명(실제 시험 문항 아님)
row.이용 시 유의사항: 라이선스, 상업적 이용, 수정·파생, 재배포, lm-eval 지원은 논문에서 확인하지 못해 '확인 불가'로 기록한다. 이용 전 공식 저장소 확인이 필요하다. 이 벤치마크는 LIBERO-Pro 과제와 여러 외부 모델·자료(VLA 모델, SAM3 등)를 바탕으로 구성되어 있으므로 각 구성 요소의 고유 약관을 따로 점검해야 한다. 실행에는 시뮬레이터와 에이전트 하니스(Codex CLI, Kimi Code CLI, Claude Code 등)가 필요하다. 논문은 시드 26, 100개 과제, 에이전트 4종 조건의 결과만 보고한다.

english_copy.axis: Agents (physical task execution with embodied skills)
english_copy.definition: A benchmark of how well LLM agents use embodied skills (133 action, 20 perception, 97 experience; 250 in total, built from 1,052 resources) to perform physical manipulation tasks in a closed observation-action loop. The evaluation set Clean100 crosses 25 LIBERO-Pro base tasks with four perturbations (language, object, task, swap), giving 100 task cases (L10 24, Goal 28, Object 24, Spatial 24). It supports three modes (native control, skill-only execution, Agent-Directed Reuse) and records success rate, actions, tokens and elapsed minutes. Paper figures are seed 26 results for four agents and are not a current global leaderboard.
english_copy.task: Clean100 (100 LIBERO-Pro task cases), comparing native control, skill-only execution, and Agent-Directed Reuse
english_copy.example: Task description, not an actual test item: for an English instruction such as "put both moka pots on the stove" (LIBERO-10, object perturbation), the agent reads scene and wrist RGB observations and calls skills or native robot controls to move the two objects in turn.

screening.paper_title: Embodied Skill Bench: Benchmarking How Well Agents with Embodied Skills Perform on Physical Tasks
screening.abstract: LLM agents increasingly control robots using VLA policies, perception models, and procedural knowledge. These modules are difficult to reuse because their interfaces, embodiment assumptions, and conditions of use differ, and their benefits on physical tasks remain unclear. We package them as embodied skills that extend agent skills with explicit embodiment assumptions and conditions of use, building 250 action, perception, and experience skills from 1,052 resources. On this basis we introduce EmbodiedSkillBench, which runs an agent in a closed observation-action loop and records success, actions, tokens, and wall-clock time. It supports three modes: native control, skill-only execution, and Agent-Directed Reuse (ADR), a mode we propose in which the agent keeps its native controls and decides for each skill whether to invoke, modify, or ignore it. Across four agents on 100 perturbed LIBERO-Pro tasks, we find that skills help an agent only as far as they exceed what it can already do. Skill-only execution lifts GPT-5.6-Sol from 11% to 63% and Kimi-K3 and Claude-Opus-5 by about 20 points, while cutting their token usage by 58% to 85%. Yet all four agents then end up between 61% and 64%, and GPT-6-Astra falls from 92% under native control to 61%. This suggests that as agents grow stronger, the role of embodied skills shifts from supplying missing capability to reducing cost: GPT-6-Astra already solves most tasks through native control, so restricting it to skills removes more than it adds. Under ADR, which lets it keep native control and call skills selectively, GPT-6-Astra recovers to 85%, within 7 points of native control, while using 14.1% fewer tokens and 11.9% less time. With Jev as a skill choosing motion directions and gripper actions, it reaches 81% with 50% fewer tokens and 57% less time. The code is available at https://github.com/HanZhi306/EmbodiedSkill-Bench.
